scenes.text: Saturn's rings are disappearing in two ways. One is an illusion. The other is *real.*
The rings stretch about 170,000 miles across, but they're only around 30 feet thick.
So every 13 to 15 years, when Earth sees them edge-on, they almost vanish. That last happened in March 2025, and next in 2038.
The real one: the rings are falling into Saturn. Sunlight and tiny meteorite hits give bits of ice an electric charge.
Then Saturn's magnetic field and gravity pull them down, as *ring* *rain.*
NASA estimates it drains enough to fill an Olympic swimming pool every half hour.
Add what Cassini saw falling in, and the rings may have less than *100* *million* *years* left.
Scientists still debate how old the rings are. But they won't last *forever.*
